title: Knowledge Check 6: Lessons 26–30
description: Fifteen questions pooled from Lessons 26–30: Integration Procedures · Data Mappers. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: How can an IP avoid re-fetching the same reference data on every run?
options: Configure caching with a sensible TTL
questions.explanation: Caching stores results for reuse, maximizing performance.

questions.question: Which data is a good caching candidate?
questions.explanation: Cache stable shared data; avoid volatile/user-specific data.

questions.question: Users see outdated data after reference data changes. What's wrong?
options: Cache TTL/scope misconfiguration or missed invalidation
questions.explanation: Stale data is the classic caching symptom. Tune TTL or invalidate.

questions.question: An IP calls an external system that may be down. How do you handle it?
options: Wrap in Try/Catch and return a controlled error
questions.explanation: Try/Catch manages failures; the Response Action returns a controlled error.

questions.question: Why place Load/write actions AFTER risky calls?
options: To avoid partial persistence. Rollback-friendly ordering
questions.explanation: Catching before writes prevents partial data and supports rollback.

questions.question: What should a Catch block do?
options: Log the failure and produce a controlled error response
questions.explanation: Catch blocks log and return predictable errors. Never silent failures.

questions.question: What defines the data an IP returns to its caller?
questions.explanation: The Response Action maps the IP's output contract.

questions.question: Why keep success and error shapes consistent?
options: So callers (FlexCards/OmniScripts) can handle both reliably
questions.explanation: Consistent contracts let UI react to success and failure alike.

questions.question: What happens if an IP has no Response Action?
options: Callers receive no defined output. The IP fails to deliver its contract
questions.explanation: The Response Action is how an IP returns data; without it the contract is broken.

questions.question: Which is an IP best practice?
options: Focused, well-named IPs with consistent contracts and error handling
questions.explanation: Best practices favor focused IPs, consistent contracts, and robust errors.

questions.question: Where should reusable data logic live?
options: In Data Mappers reused by IPs
questions.explanation: Reusing Data Mappers keeps data logic single-sourced.

questions.question: When should an IP be chainable?
options: When the process is long-running and exceeds synchronous limits
questions.explanation: Chain long processes; keep short orchestrations synchronous.

questions.question: Which Data Mapper interface is optimized for ONE object plus its related fields?
questions.explanation: Turbo Extract is optimized for single-object + related-field reads.

questions.question: Which targets can a Data Mapper produce?
options: JSON, XML, Apex class, sObject, PDF, Docusign
questions.explanation: Data Mappers target JSON, XML, Apex classes, sObjects, PDF, Docusign.
